claims.text: The initial nanoscale PtPdRhRuIrOs catalyst is a homogeneous solid solution.
Long-term durability during ethanol oxidation is enhanced by in situ formation of Pt/Pd-rich surface ensembles.
Pt/Pd-rich surface ensembles form through dynamic, reaction-induced surface segregation.
Pt/Pd-rich ensembles modify the local electronic structure to produce favorable binding energies for reaction intermediates.
The favorable intermediate binding associated with Pt/Pd-rich ensembles reduces poisoning and deactivation.
Inert-environment annealing before reaction suppresses reaction-induced surface segregation.
Under ethanol oxidation conditions, the alloy surface becomes enriched in Pt and Pd.
Pt/Pd surface segregation alters the local density of states and d-band center.
Changes in the local density of states and d-band center tune adsorption energies of key ethanol-oxidation intermediates.
Pre-annealing promotes atomic ordering and diminishes the driving forces for segregation.
Suppressing formation of Pt/Pd-rich ensembles accelerates catalyst deactivation.
Relative to the untreated baseline, the annealed catalyst will show a faster decline in catalytic current during extended ethanol oxidation.
The annealed and untreated catalysts may have similar initial activity.
The untreated baseline develops Pt/Pd surface enrichment under reaction conditions.
The proposed durability mechanism applies in acidic electrochemical ethanol oxidation from ambient temperature to approximately 80 degrees Celsius.

contradictions.description: The catalyst is described as a homogeneous or otherwise homogeneous solid solution, but the mechanism calls it intrinsically heterogeneous without clarifying whether this means compositional, electronic, or merely local configurational heterogeneity.
